Every one of them sends you a separate invoice. None of them gets called at 3 a.m. when something happens.

You do.

What keeps you up at night?

Retail
22:14 LOCAL
Parking Lot — Big Box

Two cars circling for forty minutes. Your overnight guard hasn't done a perimeter sweep in three hours. Camera 7 is pointed at a wall. A shopper just called 911 from their car. You'll hear about it on the news.

Industrial
03:11 LOCAL
Storage Yard — Fenceline

The motion sensor on the east fence has tripped eleven times tonight. Your monitoring company stopped calling after the fourth false alarm. Two thousand pounds of copper just walked out the gate. You won't know until inventory Monday.

Healthcare
02:47 LOCAL
Hospital — ED Entrance

A man with no badge walked past the lobby desk fourteen minutes ago. Your guard was on a break. He's now somewhere in the building with your staff and your patients. No one is looking for him.

Education
13:32 LOCAL
School — Side Entrance

The exterior door propped open with a brick — again. The vendor who installed your camera system says it's working. The vendor who installed your access control says it's working. Both invoices say the same thing: not my problem.

This is not a technology problem. It is an accountability vacuum.
And it is what we built Knightscope to end.
